newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU warns eastern hopefuls no favours on entry.
newsitem.headline: EU warns eastern hopefuls no favours on entry.

text.p: East European candidates to join the European Union were warned on Saturday they could not expect special favours on entry terms and that the bloc's most ambitious expansion yet could take place in several stages.
European Commission President Jacques Santer said after a brainstorming session of the EU executive that decisions on if and when to start talks with 10 eastern countries would be made objectively.
The 10 eastern European candidates could not expect friendships with individual EU countries to get them into the first round of talks, he said.

"The Commission did not exclude the possibility that the enlargement would take place in stages...Each of the candidate countries will be judged on its merits," Santer's spokesman told reporters after the meeting.
The EU executive's civil servants are currently drawing up individual reports on applications from eastern European states on the basis of tens of thousands of pages of questionnaires.
The countries are Hungary, Poland, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Bulgaria, Romania, Slovenia, Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania.
The Mediterranean islands of Malta and Cyprus are also in the queue for membership although Malta is now having second thoughts about its application after a change of government.

The spokesman said Santer concluded that the EU expansion could take place without an increase in the resources made available by existing EU members, but that the EU's institutional set-up needed overhaul to avoid paralysis.
He said the EU would have to tighten its belt when it came to allocations to EU members already receiving money to help them catch up economically.
Santer said that applicants would have to negotiate on the basis of the EU's current body of law, but would take time to fit into the EU's complex agricultural system.
